title: Protecting and Restoring NZ’s Biodiversity
attribution: Source: compdemocracy/openData, scoop-hivemind.biodiversity (154 comments moderated in, of 316). Data was gathered using the Polis software (see: compdemocracy.org/polis and github.com/compdemocracy/polis) and is sub-licensed under CC BY 4.0 with Attribution to The Computational Democracy Project. Positions, clusters and topic names come from a Delphi run on a work box on 2026-11-11 (embeddings all-MiniLM-L6-v2, UMAP, EVoC clustering; names written by the small local model qwen2.5:1.5b). It is not the run pol.is serves.

topics.name: 0_9: Conservation and Management of Game Animals

text: Comment 0: I am under 30 years of age
Comment 1: I am 30 years old or older but under 55 years of age
Comment 2: I am 55 years old or older
Comment 5: I live in a NZ town (population less than 50,000)
Comment 8: I live in a medium-sized NZ city
Comment 9: I live in a large NZ city
Comment 10: I live in a rural area in NZ
Comment 17: Aotearoa New Zealand’s biodiversity is in crisis
Comment 19: Ecosystems are interconnected and biodiversity should be managed in a coordinated way across boundaries
Comment 20: The Biodiversity Strategy should take an intergenerational view
Comment 21: The Biodiversity Strategy should encourage innovation and action, even when information is incomplete
Comment 22: The Biodiversity Strategy needs to prioritise conserving our indigenous species
Comment 23: Our physical and mental health and prosperity depends on our natural environment
Comment 24: Biodiversity management decisions need to be informed by the best available information
Comment 25: Nature has the right to exist for its own sake, regardless of any benefits we may get from it
Comment 26: More money and resources must be spent to protect and restore biodiversity and ecosystem services
Comment 27: Local, district and regional plans and/or strategies, as well as national tools (e.g. National Policy Statements and legislation) should guide action on the ground
Comment 28: We must invest in science and technology to achieve the vision and long-term outcomes of the  Biodiversity Strategy
Comment 29: The biodiversity system needs more collaborative decision-making that involves all affected parties
Comment 30: Non-indigenous ecosystems and species can be valuable for biodiversity and ecosystem services
Comment 31: Roles and responsibilities in the biodiversity system need to be better defined and communicated
Comment 32: We should prioritise research and development into alternatives to 1080 poison
Comment 33: Biodiversity management should recognise the value of mātauranga Māori and practical knowledge, right from planning through to monitoring success
Comment 34: Priority should be given to developing humane ways of eradicating pests such as possums and rats at scale
Comment 35: The Biodiversity Strategy should recognise the Treaty of Waitangi and the principles of partnership, protection and participation
Comment 36: A partnership between tangata whenua and the Crown should reflect aspirations for the co-management of nature
Comment 37: Māori must hold key roles in biodiversity governance structures
Comment 38: There is a need to consider and remove or alter any legislative blocks that prevent whānau or hapū from exercising kaitiakitanga/stewardship
Comment 39: There must be a programme in place to help Māori graduates move into roles at the Department of Conservation and other organisations
Comment 40: While indigenous biodiversity should be given priority in protected areas, the rights and incomes of property owners must not be compromised on private land
Comment 41: NZ’s economic success relies on both non-indigeneous and indigeneous species
Comment 42: Biodiversity is not just a rural issue, there are many biodiversity problems in towns and cities
Comment 43: Monitoring and evaluation of biodiversity management is crucial to ensure activities are effective and efficient
Comment 44: Allowing the private sector to compete in providing biodiversity services would make them more effective and efficient, and drive innovation
Comment 45: There are large amounts of land are in public ownership in NZ that could be used to enhance biodiversity (e.g. roadside reserves, schools)
Comment 46: Non-indigenous species and habitats can provide benefits for indigenous species
Comment 47: Healthy functioning nature is a collective good and private landowners should be compensated if they are protecting or restoring biodiversity or ecosystem services
Comment 48: It is the capitalist system, with its drive for ever increasing profits and extraction of natural resources, that is the cause of our environmental crisis

Comment 50: We need to move rapidly towards farming practices that promote sustainable food production e.g. the use of locally produced food, using techniques such as permaculture, biodynamics, urban agriculture

Comment 51: We should reduce the pressure on our biodiversity by following the advice of the World Economic Forum and other major institutions to invest in creating a circular economy that minimises waste and makes the most of resources
Comment 53: To protect and restore biodiversity and ecosystem services we must move away from a fixation on economic growth and towards sustainable production and consumption
Comment 54: By 2070, nature in Aotearoa NZ should be healthy, abundant, and thriving
Comment 55: Research into CRISPR genome editing must be looked at as a potential pest control tool.
Comment 56: Introduced species are not inherently good or bad. Their place in our biodiversity depends on the impact of the specific species.
Comment 59: Te ao Maori regarding biodiversity / the environment and science should work together. Each perspective strengthens the other.
Comment 60: Indigenous biodiversity enhancement will buffer us from the impacts of climate change.
Comment 61: The ecosystem that existed prior to 200 years ago is gone forever. All ecosystems, indigenous or not must be encouraged.
Comment 62: Restoration can't occur if destructive actions are ongoing. Stop poison spraying, land clearing, intensive farming.
Comment 64: I don't believe any level of Govt have moral ground for deciding this, as they have all allowed this to happen in the first place
Comment 69: We must continue to develop innovative ways of educating young people about our biodiversity
Comment 70: The Strategy does not address the underlying economic incentives driving the continued loss of biodiversity e.g. through urban development
Comment 73: New Vision: Current and future generations connect with Aotearoa’s’ healthy, abundant and thriving nature, restore it and are restored by it
Comment 74: Climate change adaptation should use nature-based solutions to build ecological resilience, and help maintain and restore nature
Comment 76: Government should ensure that all riparian protected areas that is manages are fenced from stock damage to vegetation and water quality
Comment 78: The protection and enhancement of our biodiversity does not have to cost huge amounts of money.
Comment 79: Please stop poisoning our lovely forests from the sky with deadly poison. Mammals and rural hunters are part of our diversity.
Comment 80: the biodiversity strategy must be measureable
Comment 81: We should innovate to become more inclusive of nature and biodiversity in our city/town designs.
Comment 87: Biodiversity values on private land can be a liability from a development perspective
Comment 88: The impacts of deer, pigs and trout need to be clearly stated and their cultural links dealt with.
Comment 89: Roadsides and other public land are currently pest plant corridors. Where possible this aspect must be eliminated.
Comment 91: Decisions on funding for pest control are made by the same people and successful innovations developed by outsiders are dismissed
Comment 92: I don't like using poisons  for pest control but necessary evil until something better is developed.
Comment 95: More focus needs to be shifted from charismatic fauna to lesser known, threatened species.
Comment 96: Biodiversity includes all life forms. In nature there are no such things as Pests. There is no such thing as being cruel to be kind.
Comment 99: The Maori perspective should not be bought, bent and manipulated in order to incorporate it into what is essentially a pakeha view.
Comment 102: The cost of monitoring the state and change of biodiversity values may exceed the cost of management
Comment 109: Farming monocultures are harmful, funding should be given to research and promote diverse  systems of farming.
Comment 111: DOC cost per dead possum is about $25, so a $10 bounty gets lots of youngsters into the bush (connections all round) solves several issues.
Comment 116: Deer/pig/trout are excellent food source, we can never get rid of them so control and use as such
Comment 120: The only way of rectifying the environmental issues is less humans. Either we control our numbers or nature will, unlikely to be "humane"
Comment 123: Ownership of water rights should not allow degradation of the resource. Stronger management, quality and quantity standards are needed.
Comment 124: Water management to prevent degradation is key to success in land and biodiversity management
Comment 128: Nature can manage itself. Humans are the cause of all perceived problems. Management is unnecessary. Leave wild places wild.
Comment 129: There needs to be a stronger emphasis on retaining our endemic invertebrate diversity. Without them our fragile ecosystem wouldn't exist.
Comment 133: Instead of focusing on protecting flagship species, we should focus on protecting entire ecosystems, which may include those species.
Comment 135: Open-data commons, curating/visualising enviro, social & financial data frm ALL users of whenua will help us make decisions democratically
Comment 136: Distributed decisions re:land use must account/forecast impact across human, social, natural, production, intellectual & financial metrics
Comment 141: More no-take marine reserves should be created, especially in the habitat of endangered animals, like Maui dolphins and endangered seabirds
Comment 142: Education standards should require educational field trips to natural spaces for all school children.
Comment 145: The biggest threat to biodiversity in our oceans and beaches is plastic pollution. We need to stop importing it, making it and buying it.
Comment 147: Allow seaweed aquaculture, which will improve biodiversity, sequester more carbon than trees and reduce ocean acidification
Comment 148: Eliminate populations of non-native species that are valued for recreational or economic reasons but that negatively impact native species e.g. tahr, trout
Comment 149: There needs to be continual shift towards the mindset that outdoor cats have a significant negative impact on native biodiversity
Comment 150: Any biodiversity strategy governance should include young people to speak for the future generations
Comment 151: We need a way to ensure enduring financial commitment of central and local government to action for the whole duration of the strategy.
Comment 161: Pest plants are a significant threat to indigenous biodiversity.  More resources and focus is needed to address this issue.
Comment 162: We need more advertising campaigns about NZ's unique flora and fauna so we feel the need to protect our species and so that we know what to do

Comment 163: Trapping for rats, etc should be fully subsidised on private property close to national and regional parks, and island sanctuaries so that native populations can expand beyond the protected areas
Comment 164: Get locals to help identify and set up as many 'mainland sanctuaries' as possible.
Comment 165: The government should direct the agriculture industry to both improve biodiversity and to develop sustainably
Comment 169: A stand-alone non-binding strategy will not be sufficient to ensure biodiversity protection
Comment 177: Preventing the illegal ownership of possums and ferrets as pets needs to be enforced more seriously.
Comment 178: There aren't enough endemic bird species being bred in captivity.
Comment 179: Prohibiting dogs from entering forests with kiwis and beaches with nesting dotterels needs to be taken more seriously.
Comment 185: There are many exciting new ways to properly engage with nature this plan isn't one of them.
Comment 186: Maori are being included in this plan because there's 1 million hectares of Maori land that needs to be poisoned.
Comment 187: For all predators to be killed off new laws will be needed to enforce this plan across all lands.
Comment 189: Many private land owners will protect native biodiversity on their land if they know how to, and are assisted/encouraged
Comment 190: The resource management act review must address cumulative adverse effects - many minor losses add up to significant losses otherwise
Comment 193: as sea level rises, we should retreat and allow native plants and animals to migrate into the space we vacate - plants and birds need it
Comment 194: We need more protection corridors that run from the sea to the mountains, managed to allow native species to thrive
Comment 195: In rural NZ, private property does not give the right to destroy specie's habitat and homes, just because you "own" the land
Comment 199: Control of most introduced bird species is inadequate.
Comment 200: Hunting of wild pigeons/kereru should never be legal again, for any race.
Comment 202: Biodiversity habitat and climate change response should go hand in hand
Comment 203: Threatened indigenous plants should be protected by stronger legal mechanisms
Comment 204: Establish a partnership between the agriculture industry and government to develop and promote farming practices that protect and restore our biodiversity
Comment 205: Man was created with domain over nature - we should use it. If it dies, it will be replaced - that's the nature of living things on earth
Comment 208: The sale and use of pesticides and herbicides should be restricted with the aim of creating a totally organic environment
Comment 210: Current commercial monoculture forestry is damaging our environment. Mixed forestry with higher value species should be promoted
Comment 211: Give nature legal personhood similar to the Whanganui River. Nature should represented by trustees appointed by iwi and the govt, and have standing in planning law and the courts.
Comment 214: Stick to trapping rather than poison in areas people can reach by foot/quad. Reduce non-target deaths by contamination of their food chain.
Comment 226: When profit is made from degrading our forest, oceans, waterways, land and air it should be taxed to fund restoration and repair
Comment 227: Conservation jobs should attract higher pay rates to attract and keep talented, knowledgeable and committed people
Comment 238: My generation has been growing watching things get worse and worse, but we are powerless to stop it, as we essentially have no voice.
Comment 241: Although consultation with stakeholders is a good idea, the democratic process as it stands is too clunky to achieve conservation success
Comment 242: Native forest soil and ground plants must be protected from browsing mammals to maintain healthy forests, water quality and reduce erosion.
Comment 243: I no longer accept that it is economy versus ecology. A healthy biodiverse environment is essential for farming sustainability.
Comment 247: We are part of nature, not separate from it. Nature has no right separate from us, but when it falls, we fall too.
Comment 248: Biodiversity and environmental stewardships are fundamental obligations of landowners.
Comment 249: This isn't a Māori-and-Pākehā issue. It's an issue for all New Zealanders needing the diverse understanding that all cultures bring.
Comment 251: Urban landscaping, such as city council plantings, need to prioritise biodiversity.
Comment 252: Home gardeners have a role to play through the plants and gardening methods that they choose.
Comment 254: Urban waterways need to be made into nature corridors and nature-compatible recreation spaces, not buried in pipes.
Comment 255: Land development must nourish the groundwater as a foundation for soil health, not drain it all to the sea.
Comment 260: Economics and business aren't the problems. Selfishness is.
Comment 266: Farmers have a lot of knowledge about land, plants and animals that needs to be valued and brought into the public conversation.
Comment 267: Urban dwellers are too far from nature to know what needs to be done. Rural voices need to be raised alongside the urban majority.
Comment 268: Scholars in all disciplines need to contribute to this work, not only scientists and engineers.
Comment 271: Golf courses could be put to much better use, increasing biodiversity in towns and making it visible.
Comment 273: Tourism must be managed to protect biodiversity.
Comment 274: Voting in Hivemind is interesting and engaging, but it takes experts to figure out what really matters.
Comment 276: Zoos should play a stronger role in educating us about biodiversity.
Comment 278: Biodiversity is too important for politicians to decide about. They need to enact what experts advise regardless of political desire.
Comment 280: Introduced species game animals (deer, tahr, chamois, etc) must be managed in partnership and consultation with the hunting community.
Comment 281: Conservation minded hunters are valuable in their contribution to management of introduced species, and their efforts should encouraged more
Comment 282: Game animals (deer, tahr, chamois, trout etc) must be recognised as a renewable source of conservation revenue, to be carefully managed.
Comment 289: Alternatives to mowed lawns need to be more acceptable. Let a bit more wilderness into gardens

Comment 290: We need to care for the foundations of the natural world (e.g. microbes, worms, beetles) and the insects, algae, lichens and other life at the bottom of the food chain, in addition to the big animals.
Comment 291: Our buildings should support biodiversity more e.g. more green walls and roofs, reuse of grey water, etc
Comment 292: Hunters spend more time in around indigenous and non-indigenous species than many other people, their advice should be sought and valued.
Comment 294: We need more trees on hillsides and coastlines to avoid erosion.
Comment 295: Iwi & small-scale land owners could use low productivity/erodible land for long-rotation totara and rimu plantations.= Habitat,fruit,timber.
Comment 296: Biodiversity needs to be defined in a way that suits Aotearoa, all of us, not a metro view, or pakeha view or rural.  We cant reverse time.
Comment 297: There should be a scheme for the trapping or shooting of wild / feral rabbits and the sale of their meat.  Far better than poisoning...
Comment 299: Muttonbirding should no longer be allowed. We need to move on from the past and look towards the future of all species.
Comment 301: More public knowledge about the science behind 1080 and the work DoC do is needed for conservation efforts to move forwards.
Comment 304: Everyone can make a difference, even if it's something small like a backyard native bird feeder or a small donation to a conservation group.
Comment 305: We need a plan to deal with cats in New Zealand.
Comment 308: We don't deserve to call ourselves Kiwis if we won't make reasonable efforts to save the Kiwi, and our other precious native species.
Comment 311: Tourists should be charged slightly more for seeing e.g. a kiwi, than a NZ citizen, and that extra money should go towards conservation.
Comment 312: Community conservation groups be better supported through more funding, better access to information and minimising paperwork
Comment 315: We should recognise and value our indigenous ecosystems for their contribution to global biodiversity. We've lost so much already
